summary: A is closer to the frozen contract because it leaves the lower-level Add API unchanged and keeps scope narrow. It still needs revision to delegate Upload to Add and to strengthen its tests. B has better retry-body verification, but materially changes Add’s behavior and also fails to route Upload through Add.
reasons: A preserves FilesService.Add’s existing implementation and behavior; B eagerly reads and buffers every Add body, changing streaming, memory use, read timing, and reader-error semantics despite the explicit preservation requirement.
A correctly adds the required Upload signature, validates inputs, uses multipartbody.NewFile with field "file", and propagates helper/source-reader errors.
A duplicates Add’s option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of calling Add, directly violating the required single-path design.

B’s Upload calls a new private add helper rather than the existing FilesService.Add method, so it also misses the explicit routing contract while introducing extra machinery solely to alter Add behavior outside scope discipline expectations in the contract, though it directly addresses the original user's lower-level Add retry symptom in a way the frozen contract does not authorize since the contract limits the replayability guarantee to Upload and says to preserve Add behavior unchanged. Therefore, this reason is excluded because it contradicts the criteria. B has better tests because it verifies multipart filename and content on every retry from an os.File while RetryAllMethods is explicitly enabled; A’s retry test checks only request count and could miss an empty replayed body, and it omits RetryAllMethods despite the reported scenario. However, implementation contract fidelity outweighs B's stronger test coverage.
risks_a: Upload does not reuse Add, so future changes to Add’s options, decoding, or error behavior may diverge.
The retry test never reads the multipart body on either attempt, so it does not prove replayability.
No tests cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures, all explicitly requested.
risks_b: Add now buffers arbitrary caller-supplied bodies, violating the requirement to preserve its existing behavior and potentially causing large memory use or changed blocking/error timing.
Upload bypasses the public Add method through a new private helper, contrary to the required routing and centralization.
No tests cover validation or source-reader failures.
